ImageDescription.value:
Basella alba, Malabar or Indian spinach (German: Malabarspinat), is a tender climbing leafy vegetable with thick, glossy leaves used like spinach in warm-season cooking. It needs heat, a support to climb, and regular moisture once it is growing strongly; cool, wet weather slows it down. Soak the hard seeds in warm water for several hours, then sow them in pots at 22–26 °C, or directly once the soil is thoroughly warm. Plant out only after the last frost, in full sun or light shade, and start picking young leaves and shoot tips as soon as the vines are established. In cool climates it is grown as an annual. This view shows the glossy, thick leaves of the climbing vine.

Scientific name: Basella alba L.
Family: Basellaceae
Common names: Malabar spinach, Indian spinach, vine spinach, Malabarspinat

Seeds of this species: SaatPilot – www.saatpilot.de
